"""dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity: exact checks.

The floor formula, kappa_s^2 (a polynomial in pi, pi bracketed by Machin's formula) and the yield
Y kappa_s = c T^3/(3 M_P^3) come from the seeding proposition's exports; every comparison of a root is
made on an integer power (xi^8 against a bound^8, eta'^8 = eta^8/xi^24, cube roots by cubes). The
per-species coefficients 1.9e-4, 1.1e-3, 2.3e-3 (scalar, fermion, vector) are the imported graviton
rate's. eta = 2.74e-8 Omega_b h^2 with Omega_b h^2 = 0.02237; baryons per entropy n_B/s = 0.1413 eta.
(i) Nine vectors: c = 9 x 2.3e-3 = 0.0207, g_d = 18, xi_floor in (3.5, 3.6) x 10^-4 at 6e14 GeV.
(ii) Mirror (premise: its content is the Standard Model's: 4 real scalars, 45 Weyl fermions, 12
vectors): c in (0.053, 0.054) with 22.5 Dirac species and (0.077, 0.078) counting 45 singly;
g_d = 4 + 45 x 7/4 + 24 = 106.75; xi_floor in (2.8, 3.2) x 10^-4 for both; eta' = eta/xi^3 in (19, 26);
eta' > 1 at c = 4 and < 1 at c = 4.1 (decreasing in c).
(iii) Y in (1.8, 2.7) x 10^-15 at the ceiling; n_B/s in (8.6, 8.7) x 10^-11; shortfall in (3, 5) x 10^4;
the rescue temperature T_desc (n_B/(s Y))^(1/3) in (1.9, 2.2) x 10^16 GeV, 31.9 to 36.2 times the
ceiling (each end of the range to that decimal);
there the floor's xi^4 equals 4 (n_B/s) g*/g_d exactly, the hot-deposit value (energy 3T per unit of
baryon number against (3/4) T s), with xi in (4.0, 4.5) x 10^-3, above eta^(1/3).
(iv) Delta N_eff of the mirror, 7.447 xi^4 with 7.447 = (8/7)(11/4)^(4/3) + 3.044 bracketed exactly:
below 1e-13 at the floor and 1e-8 at the hot deposit; per polarisation (4/7)(11/4)^(4/3) in
(2.201, 2.203), and 2.202 x 18 xi^4 below 1e-12 at the nine-vector floor.
EXPORTS: cosmo() returns the shared inputs and brackets (eta, n_B/s, xi^4 at the hot deposit, the
Delta N_eff coefficients, the mirror floor's xi^8 bracket).
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import GA
from tp_premise import premise

# --- exact bracketing helpers (rationals only) ---
def _arctan_inv(k, terms):
    """Partial sums of arctan(1/k) (alternating series): returns (lo, hi)."""
    s, lo, hi = F(0), None, None
    for j in range(terms):
        t = F((-1) ** j, (2 * j + 1) * k ** (2 * j + 1))
        s += t
        if j % 2 == 0:
            hi = s
        else:
            lo = s
    return lo, hi


def pi_bracket(terms=24):
    """Machin: pi = 16 arctan(1/5) - 4 arctan(1/239), with alternating-series brackets."""
    a_lo, a_hi = _arctan_inv(5, terms)
    b_lo, b_hi = _arctan_inv(239, terms)
    return 16 * a_lo - 4 * b_hi, 16 * a_hi - 4 * b_lo


def iroot_bracket(x, k, denom):
    """(lo, hi), multiples of 1/denom, with lo^k <= x < hi^k (integer bisection)."""
    n = x * denom ** k
    t = n.numerator // n.denominator
    lo, hi = 0, 1
    while hi ** k <= t:
        hi *= 2
    while hi - lo > 1:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if mid ** k <= t:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid
    return F(lo, denom), F(lo + 1, denom)


def exp_bracket(x, terms=40):
    """(lo, hi) with lo <= e^x <= hi for rational x, by the Taylor series with remainder."""
    if x < 0:
        lo, hi = exp_bracket(-x, terms)
        return 1 / hi, 1 / lo
    s, t = F(1), F(1)
    for j in range(1, terms + 1):
        t = t * x / j
        s += t
    bound = 3 ** (x.numerator // x.denominator + 1)
    return s, s + t * x / (terms + 1) * bound

    return dict(eta=ETA, nb_s=NB_S, c_lo=c_lo, c_hi=c_hi, gd=GD_MIRROR, xi_hot4=xi_hot4,
                floor8=(s["xi8_bracket"](c_lo, GD_MIRROR)[0], s["xi8_bracket"](c_hi, GD_MIRROR)[1]),
                photon=photon, mirror=mirror, per_pol=per_pol, seeding=s)

dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3:
"""dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3: exact checks.

Numbers of Q(pi) are Laurent polynomials in pi, {k: c} for sum c pi^k (pi transcendental, so
polynomial equality is equality of reals); decimals use rational bounds on pi. Unit-ball volumes
come from the recursion V_0 = 1, V_1 = 2, V_D = (2 pi / D) V_(D-2). The clauses C, I, S and O are
postulated; what is checked is the arithmetic and geometry the proposition derives from them.

(i)   C: the unit ball about a centre at height h above the hyperplane x_4 = 0 meets it exactly when
      h^2 <= 1 (the squared distance from the centre to the hyperplane, computed as the minimum of
      |c - x|^2 over the hyperplane, is h^2); with density 1/V_4 (R2) and one side (S), the count
      per unit three-volume is int_0^1 dh / V_4 = 1/V_4, and f_5D = (m/V_4)/(m/V_3) = V_3/V_4 =
      8/(3 pi) (R1: m cancels). Two-sided contact gives 2/V_4, so S is the factor one half.
      Which side is immaterial: in Cl(1,4) the components (1 +- omega)/2 are central orthogonal
      idempotents on which e_4 acts as +-P^-1 (the sign names a side), and two components at half
      density, each sourcing its own side, give the one-component count 1/V_4.
(ii)  Downward count on the plane x_3 = 0: rho_us/rho_3D = (1/V_3)/(1/V_2) = V_2/V_3 = 3/4; sheets
      s apart give V_3/(s V_2) read on our space, and O (equality with V_3/V_2) solves to s = 1, so
      f_3D = V_3/V_2 = 4/3. A sheet holding both modules would be sourced at 2/V_3.
(iii) The total 1 + 2 f_3D + 2 f_5D is the unit-ball rule's (11 pi + 16)/(3 pi), 5.36432 to five
      places; the unit d_b cancels from every ratio (checked at two lengths); without S the total is
      T(2) = 5.729 (three places), more than 5.5 sigma high; cubic cells give 5; the mean
      spacing V_3^(1/3) lies in (1.61, 1.62).
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

PI_LO, PI_HI = F(314159265358, 10 ** 11), F(314159265359, 10 ** 11)
OBS = F(1200, 10000) / F(2237, 100000)
SIG = F(65, 1000)
HEIGHTS = [F(0), F(1, 3), F(-3, 4), F(1), F(-1), F(7, 6), F(-5, 2), F(2)]
FOOT_SAMPLES = [[F(0), F(0), F(0)], [F(1, 2), F(-1, 3), F(2)], [F(-3), F(1), F(1, 5)]]
UNITS = [F(1), F(49, 50)]                       # two choices of the common length d_b
MASS = F(938, 7)


def lp(c, k=0):
    return {k: F(c)} if c != 0 else {}


def ladd(*xs):
    out = {}
    for x in xs:
        for k, c in x.items():
            out[k] = out.get(k, F(0)) + c
    return {k: c for k, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def lmul(*xs):
    out = {0: F(1)}
    for b in xs:
        new = {}
        for k1, c1 in out.items():
            for k2, c2 in b.items():
                new[k1 + k2] = new.get(k1 + k2, F(0)) + c1 * c2
        out = {k: c for k, c in new.items() if c != 0}
    return out


def linv(a):
    assert len(a) == 1
    (k, c), = a.items()
    return {-k: 1 / c}


def bounds(x):
    lo = hi = F(0)
    for k, c in x.items():
        u, v = c * PI_LO ** k, c * PI_HI ** k
        lo += min(u, v)
        hi += max(u, v)
    return lo, hi


def ball(D):
    V = {0: lp(1), 1: lp(2)}
    for n in range(2, D + 1):
        V[n] = lmul(lp(F(2, n), 1), V[n - 2])
    return V[D]


def prod(gens, sq):
    x = GA.sc(1)
    for i in gens:
        x = GA.mul(x, GA.gen(i), sq)
    return x


def check_five_dimensional_count():
    premise("dark-matter.nesting")
    premise("dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum")
    premise("dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball")
    met = 0
    for h in HEIGHTS:
        # squared distance from (0,0,0,h) to points (x,0) of the hyperplane; minimum at the foot x = 0
        dists = [sum(y * y for y in x) + h * h for x in FOOT_SAMPLES]
        assert min(dists) == h * h
        if h * h <= 1:
            met += 1
    assert met == 5
    # one-sided slab: the antiderivative of the constant density 1/V_4 is h/V_4, from 0 to 1
    def anti(h):
        return lmul(lp(h), linv(ball(4)))
    one_side = ladd(anti(1), lmul(lp(-1), anti(0)))
    two_side = ladd(anti(1), lmul(lp(-1), anti(-1)))
    f5 = lmul(lp(MASS), one_side, linv(lmul(lp(MASS), linv(ball(3)))))
    assert f5 == {-1: F(8, 3)}
    assert lmul(two_side, linv(one_side)) == {0: F(2)}
    return True


def check_side_is_immaterial():
    premise("dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra")
    premise("dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball")
    sq = GA.sig(1, 4)
    P, w = prod([0, 1, 2, 3], sq), prod([0, 1, 2, 3, 4], sq)
    Pinv = GA.scal(-1, P)                                   # P^2 = -1
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(P, P, sq), GA.sc(-1))
    ep = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), w))
    em = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(GA.sc(1), w))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(ep, em, sq), {}) and GA.eq(GA.add(ep, em), GA.sc(1))
    assert all(GA.commutes(ep, GA.gen(i), sq) for i in range(5))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.gen(4), ep, sq), GA.mul(Pinv, ep, sq))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.gen(4), em, sq), GA.scal(-1, GA.mul(Pinv, em, sq)))
    half = lmul(lp(F(1, 2)), linv(ball(4)))
    assert ladd(half, half) == lmul(lp(1), linv(ball(4)))
    return True


def check_three_dimensional_sheets():
    premise("dark-matter.nesting")
    premise("dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum")
    premise("dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball")
    premise("dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones")
    down = lmul(linv(ball(3)), linv(linv(ball(2))))          # (1/V_3)/(1/V_2)

def fock(m, extra=0):

    v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(m + i))) for i in range(m)]

def det(M):
    M = [row[:] for row in M]
    n, d = len(M), F(1)
    for c in range(n):
        p = next((r for r in range(c, n) if M[r][c] != 0), None)
        if p is None:
            return F(0)
        if p != c:
            M[c], M[p] = M[p], M[c]
            d = -d
        d *= M[c][c]
        for r in range(c + 1, n):
            t = M[r][c] / M[c][c]
            M[r] = [a - t * b for a, b in zip(M[r], M[c])]

def ip(sq, a, b):
    return sum(F(sq[k]) * a[k] * b[k] for k in range(len(sq)))


def refl(sq, a):
    Qa = ip(sq, a, a)
    return lambda x: [x[k] - 2 * ip(sq, x, a) / Qa * a[k] for k in range(len(sq))]


def standard_pair(sq):
    i = sq.index(1)
    j = sq.index(-1)

    t = -2 * ip(sq, u0, d) / ip(sq, d, d)

    c = ip(sq, u, w)
    x = [w[k] - ip(sq, w, w) / (2 * c) * u[k] for k in range(len(sq))]

def ssyt(shape, n):
    """Content vectors of the semistandard tableaux of the given shape with entries 0..n-1."""
    cells = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(shape) for c in range(row)]
    out = Counter()

    def fill(i, T):
        if i == len(cells):

            for v in T.values():
                cont[v] += 1
            out[tuple(cont)] += 1
            return
        r, c = cells[i]
        lo = 0
        if c > 0:
            lo = max(lo, T[(r, c - 1)])
        if r > 0:
            lo = max(lo, T[(r - 1, c)] + 1)
        for v in range(lo, n):
            T[(r, c)] = v
            fill(i + 1, T)
            del T[(r, c)]

    fill(0, {})
    return out

def sample_vectors(m):

            GA.add(GA.scal(3, GA.gen(m - 1)), GA.gen(m))]


def fock(m, extra=0):
    sq = tuple([1] * m + [-1] * m + [1] * extra)
    w = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(m + i))) for i in range(m)]
    v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(m + i))) for i in range(m)]
    f = GA.sc(1)
    for x in w:

    I = GA.sc(1)
    for i in range(2 * m):
        I = GA.mul(I, GA.gen(i), sq)
    return sq, w, v, f, I


def prod(xs, sq):
    y = GA.sc(1)
    for x in xs:

def fock_states(m, v, f, sq):
    """v_S f for S subsets of {0..m-1}, ordered by S; Fock grade |S|."""
    out = []

def mono(c, k=0):

    for k in range(n + 1):

dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower:
"""dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can: exact checks.

Everything is computed in GA.py (exact Fractions). For a diagonal signature (p,q):
- the centre is the span of the central basis blades (commutation with a generator acts on a blade by a
  sign, so the centre is spanned by blades); its dimension and omega^2 give the component count;
- a primitive idempotent f = prod (1 + e_T)/2 is built greedily from commuting blades of square +1 that
  lower dim Cl f, and primitivity is then certified independently: the corner f Cl f is a division
  algebra, read off from the signature of its regular trace form tr(L_xy) ((1,0) = R, (1,1) = C,
  (1,3) = H; any other signature is not a division algebra);
- the irreducible module is Cl f, of real dimension m d, and m^2 d (components) = 2^n is checked.
Checked: the type table D and the component count on the P3 representatives (premise: the census and
sort of towers-are-residues), and residue invariance on all twenty signatures with n <= 5, including
along every rung (p,q) -> (p+1,q+1) (premise: the eight-towers fact). (i)-(iii): the intrinsic group is
the unit group of D; its Lie algebra is the trace-free (pure) part of f Cl f, of dimension 0, 1, 3, on
which x^2 = -N(x) f with N positive definite (so the complex structures are +-J for C and the unit
sphere S^2 of pure quaternions for H). (iv): at r = 1, 5 the central idempotents (1 +- omega)/2 give two
modules on which omega acts as +1 and -1 (inequivalent: omega is central); at r = 3, 7 omega f lies in
f Cl f, is pure and squares to -f: the volume element is the complex unit.
The literature classification (rule2.imported-classification-centre-type-c-external) is recomputed,
not relied on, so it gets no premise() call.
EXPORTS["clifford_type"](p, q) returns the dict computed here, for dependent checks.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import GA
from pyutil import get_or_set
from tp_premise import premise

P3_REPS = {6: (1, 3), 2: (3, 1), 0: (2, 2), 4: (4, 0), 1: (2, 1), 7: (1, 2), 3: (4, 1), 5: (1, 4)}
_CACHE = {}


def _coords(x, blades):
    return [x.get(b, F(0)) for b in blades]


def _blade_sq(b, sq):
    return GA.mul({b: F(1)}, {b: F(1)}, sq).get((), F(0))


def _solve_in(basis_rows, v):
    """Coordinates of v in the span of the independent rows (exact), or None."""
    d = len(basis_rows)
    M = [[basis_rows[i][k] for i in range(d)] + [v[k]] for k in range(len(v))]
    ker = GA.field_kernel(M)
    for kv in ker:
        if kv[d] != 0:
            return [-kv[i] / kv[d] for i in range(d)]
    return None


def clifford_type(p, q):
    if (p, q) in _CACHE:
        return _CACHE[(p, q)]
    n = p + q
    sq = GA.sig(p, q)
    blades = GA.all_blades(n)
    central = [b for b in blades if all(GA.commutes({b: F(1)}, GA.gen(i), sq) for i in range(n))]
    om = tuple(range(n))
    w2 = _blade_sq(om, sq)

    def dim_left(f):
        return GA.rank_of_vectors([_coords(GA.mul({b: F(1)}, f, sq), blades) for b in blades])
    f, dim, chosen = GA.sc(1), 2 ** n, []
    for b in blades:
        if b == () or _blade_sq(b, sq) != 1:
            continue
        if not all(GA.commutes({b: F(1)}, {c: F(1)}, sq) for c in chosen):
            continue
        f2 = GA.mul(f, GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), {b: F(1)})), sq)
        d2 = dim_left(f2)
        if 0 < d2 < dim:
            f, dim, chosen = f2, d2, chosen + [b]
    # corner algebra f A f
    rows, corner = [], []
    for b in blades:
        y = GA.mul(GA.mul(f, {b: F(1)}, sq), f, sq)
        c = _coords(y, blades)
        if any(c) and GA.rank_of_vectors(rows + [c]) > len(rows):
            rows.append(c)
            corner.append(y)
    d = len(corner)
    # regular representation L_x on the corner and the trace form
    L = []
    for x in corner:
        L.append([_solve_in(rows, _coords(GA.mul(x, y, sq), blades)) for y in corner])

    def lmat(cx):
        return [[sum((cx[a] * L[a][j][i] for a in range(d)), F(0)) for j in range(d)] for i in range(d)]
    prods = [[_solve_in(rows, _coords(GA.mul(x, y, sq), blades)) for y in corner] for x in corner]
    T = [[sum(lmat(prods[i][j])[k][k] for k in range(d)) for j in range(d)] for i in range(d)]
    tsig = GA.congruence_signature(T)
    D = {(1, 0, 0): "R", (1, 1, 0): "C", (1, 3, 0): "H"}.get(tuple(tsig))
    comps = 2 if (len(central) == 2 and w2 == 1) else 1
    m = dim // d if D else None
    out = dict(sig=(p, q), r=(p - q) % 8, centre=len(central), omega2=w2, D=D, d=d, comps=comps,
               m=m, dimS=dim, f=f, corner=corner, rows=rows, sq=sq, trace=T, tsig=tsig)
    _CACHE[(p, q)] = out
    return out


def _pure_part(t):
    """Trace-free part of the corner, as coordinate vectors: kernel of x -> tr(L_x) = T[x][unit]."""
    d = t["d"]
    unit = _solve_in(t["rows"], _coords(t["f"], GA.all_blades(sum(t["sig"]))))
    row = [sum(t["trace"][i][j] * unit[j] for j in range(d)) for i in range(d)]
    return GA.field_kernel([row]), unit


def check_type_table_on_p3_representatives():
    premise("dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter")
    want_D = {0: "R", 1: "R", 2: "R", 3: "C", 4: "H", 5: "H", 6: "H", 7: "C"}
    want_comps = {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 1, 5: 2, 6: 1, 7: 1}
    ok = True
    for r, (p, q) in P3_REPS.items():
        t = clifford_type(p, q)
        ok = ok and t["r"] == r and t["D"] == want_D[r] and t["comps"] == want_comps[r]
        ok = ok and t["comps"] * t["m"] * t["m"] * t["d"] == 2 ** (p + q)
        ok = ok and (t["centre"] == 2) == (r % 2 == 1)
    ok = ok and clifford_type(0, 4)["D"] == "H" and clifford_type(0, 4)["comps"] == 1
    GA.check("thm:types: D = R (r = 0, 1, 2), C (3, 7), H (4, 5, 6); two components exactly at r = 1, 5", ok)
    return ok


def check_type_is_a_residue_invariant():
    premise("dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock")
    by_res = {}
    ok = True
    count = 0
    for n in range(1, 6):
        for p in range(n + 1):
            t = clifford_type(p, n - p)
            ok = ok and t["D"] is not None
            ok = ok and t["comps"] * t["m"] * t["m"] * t["d"] == 2 ** n
            get_or_set(by_res, t["r"], set()).add((t["D"], t["comps"]))
            if p >= 1 and n - p >= 1:
                lower = clifford_type(p - 1, n - p - 1) if n >= 3 else None
                if lower is not None:
                    ok = ok and (lower["D"], lower["comps"]) == (t["D"], t["comps"])
            count += 1
    ok = ok and count == 20 and len(by_res) == 8 and all(len(v) == 1 for v in by_res.values())
    GA.check("thm:types: on all 20 signatures with n <= 5 (D, components) depends on p - q mod 8 only, "
             "and is unchanged along each rung (p,q) -> (p+1,q+1)", ok)
    return ok


def _scalar_multiple(s, f):
    """lam with s = lam f (f nonzero), or None."""
    b0 = next(iter(f))
    lam = s.get(b0, F(0)) / f[b0]
    return lam if GA.eq(s, GA.scal(lam, f)) else None


def check_intrinsic_groups():
    premise("dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter")
    want_pure = {0: 0, 2: 0, 3: 1, 7: 1, 4: 3, 5: 3, 6: 3}
    ok = True
    for r, dim_pure in want_pure.items():
        t = clifford_type(*P3_REPS[r])
        pure, unit = _pure_part(t)
        ok = ok and len(pure) == dim_pure and len(pure) == t["d"] - 1
        sq = t["sq"]
        X = [GA.add(*[GA.scal(c[i], t["corner"][i]) for i in range(t["d"]) if c[i] != 0]) for c in pure]
        G = []
        for a in X:
            row = []
            for b in X:
                s = GA.scal(F(-1, 2), GA.add(GA.mul(a, b, sq), GA.mul(b, a, sq)))
                lam = _scalar_multiple(s, t["f"])
                ok = ok and lam is not None
                row.append(lam if lam is not None else F(0))
            G.append(row)
        if dim_pure:
            ok = ok and tuple(GA.congruence_signature(G)) == (dim_pure, 0, 0)
    GA.check("intrinsic groups: the pure part of D has dimension 0 (Z2 at r = 0, 2), 1 (U(1) at r = 3, 7), "
             "3 (Sp(1) at r = 4, 5, 6), with x^2 = -N(x) f, N positive definite", ok)
    return ok


def check_volume_element_on_the_odd_residues():
    premise("dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter")
    ok = True
    for r in (1, 5):
        p, q = P3_REPS[r]
        n = p + q
        sq = GA.sig(p, q)
        om = {tuple(range(n)): F(1)}
        t = clifford_type(p, q)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(om, om, sq), GA.sc(1)) and t["comps"] == 2
        # f and its grade involute lie in the two components; omega is central
        signs = []
        for g in (t["f"], GA.grade_inv(t["f"])):
            lam = _scalar_multiple(GA.mul(om, g, sq), g)
            ok = ok and lam is not None and GA.eq(GA.mul(g, g, sq), g)
            signs.append(lam)
        ok = ok and sorted(signs) == [-1, 1]
        for s in (1, -1):
            P = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), GA.scal(s, om)))
            ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(P, P, sq), P) and all(GA.commutes(P, GA.gen(i), sq) for i in range(n))
    for r in (3, 7):
        p, q = P3_REPS[r]
        n = p + q
        sq = GA.sig(p, q)
        om = {tuple(range(n)): F(1)}
        t = clifford_type(p, q)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(om, om, sq), GA.sc(-1)) and t["comps"] == 1
        J = GA.mul(om, t["f"], sq)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.mul(t["f"], om, sq), t["f"], sq), J)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(J, J, sq), GA.scal(-1, t["f"]))
        ok = ok and _solve_in(t["rows"], _coords(J, GA.all_blades(n))) is not None and t["D"] == "C"
    GA.check("(iv): r = 1, 5: omega^2 = 1, two modules with omega = +1 and -1; r = 3, 7: omega f is the "
             "complex unit of f Cl f (square -f)", ok)
    return ok


EXPORTS = {"clifford_type": clifford_type, "P3_REPS": P3_REPS}
dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow:

(a) Who carries: every signature of an odd residue is odd-dimensional (p - q and p + q have one
parity), so by the flag-bit theorem no odd residue is oriented, on any window. The even residues'

r = 0 has two ((2,2)). Oriented and causal: {2, 6}.
(b) The fork (2,2), in GA.py: the ambient R^(3,3) has omega^2 = +1 (no complex unit in its centre); a
primitive idempotent f of the even subalgebra Cl^0(3,3), built greedily from commuting even blades of
square +1, has Cl^0 f of real dimension 4 and corner f Cl^0 f = R (one-dimensional), the real
four-component spinors; three mutually orthogonal null vectors e_i + e_(3+i) span U with
dim U^perp = 6 - 3 (three pairs, the maximum). Cl^0(2,2): its pseudoscalar is central in it with square
+1, splitting it into two four-dimensional ideals (the two SL(2,R) factors).
(c) Mass begins at two: with a small exact polynomial ring, det(pi1 pt1^T) = 0 identically and
det(pi1 pt1^T + pi2 pt2^T) = <pi1 pi2><pt1 pt2> as a polynomial identity in the eight coordinates.
The Standard-Model gauge algebra on the fork (standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse) is cited,
not computed: no premise() call for it.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import GA
from tp_premise import premise

SIGS = [(p, q) for p in range(11) for q in range(11) if 1 <= p + q <= 10]

# --- a minimal multivariate polynomial ring over Q: {exponent tuple: Fraction} ---
NV = 8


def var(i):
    e = [0] * NV
    e[i] = 1
    return {tuple(e): F(1)}


def padd(a, b, s=1):
    out = dict(a)
    for k, v in b.items():
        out[k] = out.get(k, F(0)) + s * v
    return {k: v for k, v in out.items() if v != 0}


def pmul(a, b):
    out = {}
    for k1, v1 in a.items():
        for k2, v2 in b.items():
            k = tuple(x + y for x, y in zip(k1, k2))
            out[k] = out.get(k, F(0)) + v1 * v2
    return {k: v for k, v in out.items() if v != 0}


def even_corner(p, q):
    n = p + q
    sq = GA.sig(p, q)
    ev = [b for b in GA.all_blades(n) if len(b) % 2 == 0]

    def co(x):
        return [x.get(b, F(0)) for b in ev]

    def dim_left(f):
        return GA.rank_of_vectors([co(GA.mul({b: F(1)}, f, sq)) for b in ev])
    f, dim, chosen = GA.sc(1), len(ev), []
    for b in ev:
        if b and GA.mul({b: F(1)}, {b: F(1)}, sq) == {(): F(1)} and \
                all(GA.commutes({b: F(1)}, {c: F(1)}, sq) for c in chosen):
            f2 = GA.mul(f, GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), {b: F(1)})), sq)
            d2 = dim_left(f2)
            if 0 < d2 < dim:
                f, dim, chosen = f2, d2, chosen + [b]
    corner = GA.rank_of_vectors([co(GA.mul(GA.mul(f, {b: F(1)}, sq), f, sq)) for b in ev])
    return f, dim, corner


def check_oriented_and_causal_towers():
    premise("dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension")
    premise("dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter")
    ok = all(((p - q) % 2) == ((p + q) % 2) for p, q in SIGS)
    odd_dims = {r: {p + q for p, q in SIGS if (p - q) % 8 == r} for r in (1, 3, 5, 7)}
    ok = ok and all(all(d % 2 == 1 for d in ds) for ds in odd_dims.values())
    p3 = {r: sorted(s for s in SIGS if sum(s) == 4 and (s[0] - s[1]) % 8 == r) for r in (0, 2, 4, 6)}
    oriented = sorted(r for r in p3 if all((p + q) % 4 == 0 for p, q in p3[r]))
    times = {r: sorted({min(p, q) for p, q in p3[r]}) for r in p3}
    ok = ok and oriented == [0, 2, 4, 6] and times == {0: [2], 2: [1], 4: [0], 6: [1]}
    both = sorted(r for r in oriented if 1 in times[r])
    ok = ok and both == [2, 6]
    GA.check("cor:whocarries: odd residues odd-dimensional (never oriented); even P3 representatives "
             "four-dimensional; oriented and causal exactly {2, 6}", ok)
    return ok


def check_fork_conformal_spinors_are_real():
    sq = GA.sig(3, 3)
    om = {tuple(range(6)): F(1)}
    ok = GA.eq(GA.mul(om, om, sq), GA.sc(1))
    f, dim, corner = even_corner(3, 3)

    # three mutually orthogonal null vectors, and U^perp of dimension 3
    us = [[F(1) if k in (i, 3 + i) else F(0) for k in range(6)] for i in range(3)]
    ip = lambda a, b: sum(F(sq[k]) * a[k] * b[k] for k in range(6))

    perp = 6 - GA.rank_of_vectors([[F(sq[k]) * u[k] for k in range(6)] for u in us])
    ok = ok and perp == 3
    # Cl^0(2,2): the pseudoscalar is central in the even part and squares to +1
    sq22 = GA.sig(2, 2)
    om4 = {(0, 1, 2, 3): F(1)}
    ev = [b for b in GA.all_blades(4) if len(b) % 2 == 0]

        ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors([[GA.mul(P, {b: F(1)}, sq22).get(c, F(0)) for c in ev] for b in ev]) == 4
    GA.check("fork: Cl(3,3) has omega^2 = +1; Cl^0(3,3) f has dimension 4 with corner R; three pairs; Cl^0(2,2) "
             "splits into two four-dimensional ideals", ok)
    return ok


def check_mass_begins_at_two_on_the_fork():

    t1 = [var(2), var(3)]
